event_note: Company IR (investor.urbn.com, urbanoutfittersinc.gcs-web.com) returned 403 on every page tried, so this is not confirmed from a company document. Earnings Whispers marks the date CONFIRMED for 2026-11-24 after the close, 4:05 PM ET (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/URBN). OptionsAI also lists Nov 24 after the close (https://tools.optionsai.com/companies/URBN/earnings/neutral-trades). The front weekly (2026-11-27) carries an event-sized straddle, and last year's Q3 came on the same Tuesday at 5 p.m. ET. Session: amc. conviction_note: The evidence nets to about zero. Same-day peer prints (ANF +21% on a +6% comp and a raise, DKS, KSS, BBY all beat and raised) and a bar that sits at the company's own guide arithmetic point up. Gap's soft October / early November, the October Census clothing dip, Buckle's negative October comp, an 8.3% five-day run-up to within 3% of the 52-week high and mildly put-paid skew point down. abs_move is set near the 9.97% implied move (the last eight prints ran 0.8-22.8% with a median of about 6.6%), and p_up is 53, so the scaled number (+0.57) and impact_sum (+0.4) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 FY27 consensus EPS $1.53 and revenue $1.67B, two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/URBN, whisper $1.61) and Benzinga's earnings table via search snippet. Other sources: StockMarketWatch $1.52; Chartmill $1.56 / $1.699B (fetch 403, snippet only). Company guide from the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 2026, https://www.retaildive.com/news/nuuly-rental-urban-outfitters-second-quarter-earnings/829128/ and https://quartr.com/events/urban-outfitters-inc-urbn-q2-2027_3gP8gksU): total sales up high single digits, retail comps up mid single digits (FP Group HSD, UO MSD, Anthropologie LSD-MSD), Nuuly up high-20s, wholesale up low teens, gross margin up 25-50bp, SG&A growing slightly below sales, tax 24.75%. Against Q3 FY26 sales of $1,529.4M (Zacks), +9% is $1.667B, so revenue consensus sits at the top of the HSD guide. My guide arithmetic gives about $1.51-1.52 EPS at +9% sales, so EPS consensus is at or a touch above the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 7,613,290 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 8.68 days to cover, up from 6.85M in mid-August (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/urbn/short-interest). That is about 8.9% of shares outstanding and more of free float, since the Hayne family holds a large block (Form 4, 17.3M shares direct). The 2026-11-13 settlement publishes today and was not seen. Skew_25d +2.74 vol points (mild downside paid). Put/call OI 2.07 on thin OI of 1,474. ATM spread 39% of mid, so the 9.97% implied move is indicative only. Tape: +8.32% over 5 days, -1.45% over 20 days, 3% below the 52-week high. A moderately crowded short sits into a stock already bid up into the print.

findings.finding: Abercrombie & Fitch reported this morning (2026-11-24) for the same Aug-Oct quarter: comparable sales +6% (Americas +5%, Hollister +5%), sales +11%. It raised FY guidance to ~6% sales growth and $13.70-13.90 EPS (from $13.10-13.60), guided Q4 sales ~+7%, and the stock rose about 21-25% intraday. A young-apparel peer printing after URBN last spoke points to healthy Q3 and holiday-start demand for UO/FP's customer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: URBN rose ~13.5% the day after its Q3 FY26 print on a beat plus a strong Q4 outlook (OptionsAI history), in a season when peers were also strong. There is no measured history of URBN's sympathy moves to ANF.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already. The 18:08 UTC sealed spot sits within today's session, and URBN's 5-day +8.3% likely includes some sympathy. If fully priced, URBN would trade well through its 52-week high and the straddle would have compressed, but it is still 3% below the high with ~10% implied. What is not priced is URBN's own confirmation that demand held into November.
findings.independence: CNBC movers page (https://cnbc.com/2026/11/24/stocks-moving-the-most-today-live-updates.html) confirms ANF +21%. Different source, same event.

findings.finding: Breadth of retail beats and raises on 2026-11-24: Dick's +16% (EPS $1.94 vs $1.40, FY guide raised), Kohl's +7% premarket (sales $3.5B beat, FY guide raised), Best Buy +3% (comp +6.1%, best in five years). CNBC notes retailers bucked a broader market decline. This is a consumer-spend read into the holiday quarter URBN will guide on tonight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: URBN's two largest recent upside reactions (+22.8% May 2025, +13.5% Nov 2025, per OptionsAI) both came with outlooks above the Street.
findings.why_not_priced: These are macro-to-company proxies from different categories (sporting goods, department store, electronics). The market will not credit URBN's Q4 guide until URBN gives it.
findings.independence: Proxy only, from a different document than ANF (finding 1). Both point to a strong retail tape today.

findings.finding: Gap Inc. (Q3 release 2026-11-19) said 'demand softened in October and early November, amidst warmer weather' and cited a 'slower than expected start to the fourth quarter'. It cut FY sales to roughly flat (from +1-1.5%), guided Q4 sales flat to -1%, and assumed incremental tariffs rising from ~10% to 'high-teens' for the rest of its year. October is the last month of URBN's Q3 and early November is the start of its Q4, so this is a risk to URBN's Q4 guide and margin commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: URBN fell ~5% after the Aug 2026 Q2 print (OptionsAI) and -10.65% after Aug 2025 despite beats, on outlook and markdown worries. URBN sells guidance disappointment.
findings.why_not_priced: Gap printed five days ago and URBN rose 8.3% over those five days, so the market did not mark URBN down for it. If it were priced, URBN would have lagged the group into the print. Gap is a value/mall peer with a different customer, and ANF (finding 1) contradicts it for the young-adult segment, so this is sized below that peer.
findings.independence: Census October clothing-store sales and Buckle's October comp (finding 4) point the same way on October softness, from different sources.

findings.finding: Independent series on October: advance Census retail sales at clothing and accessory stores fell to $26,377M in October 2026 from $26,575M in September (-0.75% m/m, seasonally adjusted, released 2026-11-17). Buckle's October comp was -0.5% (Q3 comp +0.6%). The last month of URBN's Q3 was soft across the category.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured URBN reaction to category data; URBN comps have diverged from the category before (HSD-plus growth in 2025-26 against a low-single-digit category).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a broad proxy. URBN has grown well above the category for eight straight record quarters, so the market reasonably discounts it. One of three months, and a seasonally adjusted m/m dip, not a y/y decline.
findings.independence: Buckle October 2026 sales release (https://finviz.com/news/416668/the-buckle-inc-reports-october-2026-net-sales, 2026-11-05) is a separate document. Gap (finding 3) agrees.

findings.finding: Revenue consensus of $1.67B is +9.2% on Q3 FY26's $1,529.4M, at the top of a 'high single digit' guide. URBN delivered +10.4% in Q2 FY27 against a comparable HSD framework, and revenue beat ($1.66B vs $1.65B). EPS consensus of $1.53 is about at my guide arithmetic (~$1.51-1.52), while the Earnings Whispers whisper is $1.61. The bar is set at the guide rather than above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27: EPS in line at $1.72, revenue +0.6% beat, stock fell ~5% (OptionsAI; allinvestview shows a different day's +4%, so the sign is disputed). Q3 FY26: EPS $1.28 vs $1.19, stock +13.5%. URBN pays for a real beat plus a guide, not for an in-line print.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper ($1.61) already sits above consensus, so a modest beat is expected. This finding only says the printed bar is not stretched. It is small because the beat is the base case.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers bar (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/URBN). Q3 FY26 base from Zacks via search snippet. The guide is from the same Aug call as finding 8.

findings.finding: URBN rose 8.32% over the 5 sessions into the print (baseline tape) to 3% below its 52-week high. The 20-day change is -1.45%, so the run-up is recent and coincides with the peer beat-and-raise tape (ANF, DKS today). The bar for the Q4 guide has risen inside a week.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2 FY27 (Aug 2026) the stock fell ~5% on an in-line print having been bid up; after Aug 2025, -10.65% on a beat. Beats with an unremarkable guide have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding is that the run-up raises the bar the guide must clear, and that a 2.74-point put skew with 2.07 put/call OI says hedgers agree.
findings.independence: Skew +2.74 and put/call OI 2.07 in the same baseline. Same document, so this counts once.

findings.finding: Short interest is 7.61M shares (2026-10-30), 8.68 days to cover, about 8.9% of shares outstanding and a larger share of free float given the Hayne family block. It rose from 6.85M in mid-August, so a beat-and-raise has squeeze fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +13.5% (Nov 2025) and +22.8% (May 2025) upside reactions are consistent with short covering on strong guides.
findings.why_not_priced: Days to cover near 9 is not visible in the straddle. It skews the realised distribution to the upside only if the guide is good, so it is small.
findings.independence: Search snippets from fintel (10.7% of float, undated) and Benzinga (11.8%, undated) point the same way but are stale.

findings.finding: The Q2 FY27 gross margin was up only 4bp despite tariffs, fuel surcharges and higher markdowns at Anthropologie. Anthropologie was guided to the lowest Q3 comp of the three brands (low-to-mid single digit, after +3.0% in Q2), and inventory was +11.8% y/y against +10.4% sales. That is a markdown risk to the 25-50bp Q3 gross margin guide, in a segment worth about 37% of sales. FP Group (HSD guide, +10% Q2 comp) and Nuuly (+29%) would have to falter too for the total to miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2025: -10.65% on an inventory build despite a beat (inventory +15.1% then). URBN is sensitive to inventory and markdown lines.
findings.why_not_priced: This was public in August and the guide already embeds it. It matters only if October's warm weather (Gap) left Anthropologie fall/outerwear heavy. Sized net of the rest of the company.
findings.independence: allinvestview summary (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/URBN/q2-2027/) separately cites higher Anthropologie markdowns.

findings.finding: URBN booked a $100.1M IEEPA tariff refund in Q2 FY27, excluded from adjusted EPS. ANF booked a further ~$20M of IEEPA refunds in its Aug-Oct quarter, so URBN may book more refunds in Q3. That would be a GAAP one-off with no path to the adjusted guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY27 refund ($2.78 GAAP vs $1.72 adjusted) came with a ~5% decline. The market looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is excluded from the adjusted figures the stock trades on. It is worth something only via cash and buyback capacity.
findings.independence: ANF 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018840/000101884026000052/q32026pressrelease.htm) shows the refund flow continuing in the Aug-Oct quarter.

findings.finding: Nuuly is expanding East Coast fulfilment (Falls Township, PA, ~975k sq ft), taking East Coast capacity from ~200k to ~600k subscribers on a path to ~1.2M total. Subscribers topped 500k in June and Nuuly is guided to +high-20s in Q3. A capacity-backed Nuuly outlook for FY28 could feature in tonight's commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nuuly growth of +49% was a cited driver of the Nov 2025 +13.5% reaction (search snippet from finviz recap of that print).
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (Supply Chain Dive article id 829575, August 2026 earnings coverage)
findings.why_not_priced: This has been public since June/August and the high-20s guide is known. Upside only if management raises its subscriber trajectory. Small.
findings.independence: Retail Dive Q2 coverage (https://www.retaildive.com/news/nuuly-rental-urban-outfitters-second-quarter-earnings/829128/) gives the 1.2M-subscriber target. Same company source.

findings.finding: Insider activity in Q3/Q4-to-date is routine. Director Harry Cherken sold 5,000 shares at $92.12 on 2026-10-29 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-04-17. Richard/Margaret Hayne gifted 60,000 shares on 2026-11-02 (17.3M held after). There were no open-market purchases.
findings.why_not_priced: These are plan sales and gifts and carry no information. Filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Pending USTR Section 301 'excess capacity' investigation (15 countries + EU) could raise apparel tariffs further. No dated outcome, so this is a risk to FY28 margins, not to this print. Gap's 'high-teens incremental' assumption suggests peers are budgeting for it.

baseline_tension: The evidence is balanced. The peer beat-and-raise tape and a bar at the guide cut mildly against the +2.74 put skew. Gap/Census October softness and an 8.3% five-day run-up agree with it. p_up stays at 53 rather than higher because the run-up has partly priced the peer read.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, ~8.7 days to cover): shrank the negatives that rest on positioning or proxies. Run-up -1.0 to -0.8; Gap -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is small and loses to a direct peer): retail-breadth proxy +0.5 to +0.4, Census/Buckle -0.5 to -0.4. ANF, a direct peer printing after URBN last spoke, is kept at +1.0.
Lesson 9 (a segment finding is sized net of the rest): Anthropologie markdowns -0.5 to -0.3, since FP Group and Nuuly carry the total.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the IEEPA refund +0.2 to +0.1, as it has no path to the adjusted guide.
Lesson 6 (bar): bar verified at two agreeing sources ($1.53 / $1.67B) plus the company guide, so no cap was applied. p_up moved 52 to 53 because the negatives shrank.
